title: Beef, ground, 80% lean meat / 20% fat, raw

content.title: About
content.content: Ground beef with 80% lean meat and 20% fat is raw meat obtained by grinding beef. It has a characteristic meaty aroma, a soft texture, and is used in a wide range of dishes, from patties to sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ground beef is a staple in many national cuisines, from American burgers to Italian ragù.
The 20% fat content provides a balance between juiciness and moderate calorie density.
Ground beef can be classified as lean (up to 10% fat) or higher‑fat (30% and above) – 20% is considered optimal for most recipes.
When stored properly in the refrigerator, raw ground beef stays fresh for up to 2 days, and up to 3 months in the freezer.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Ground beef is an excellent source of complete protein, essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Beef provides heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Source of zinc
items.content: Zinc supports immune function and participates in protein metabolism.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The meat supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, important for energy production.

items.title: Moderate fat content
items.content: The 20% fat gives dishes juiciness without making them overly calorie‑dense.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Raw meat can harbor pathogens such as E. coli and Salmonella; thorough cooking is required.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: While 20% fat is moderate, high intake of saturated fats may affect cholesterol levels.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef.

items.title: Storage
items.content: Ground beef spoils quickly if not kept cold; it should be stored at ≤ 4 °C.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Ground beef is suitable for making patties, meatballs, sauces, fillings for pies, lasagna, tacos, and many other dishes. If a leaner result is desired, excess fat can be drained after cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the meat in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator for no more than 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in freezer bags at –18 °C, where it remains good for up to 3 months. Thaw in the refrigerator before use.
